assumptions: all result-producing reads are prospectively declared or blocked
teaching_traceability.falsifier_or_refusal: An unknown read, unpinned dependency, or branch on a run-metadata property fails before any state advance.
teaching_traceability.honest_nonclaim: Matching hashes does not prove the scientific model is true.
teaching_traceability.math_or_proof: If property p can select value/branch/order/arithmetic/failure/row/terminal state, p is in S and enters H_sem; R is disjoint and cannot select science: S intersection R = empty.
teaching_traceability.ordinary_example: A recipe's ingredient amounts affect the cake; the kitchen's street address identifies the occasion but should not change the recipe.
teaching_traceability.plain_meaning: Inputs that can change science are frozen into execution semantics; host names and clocks remain run facts.
teaching_traceability.positive_value: A later reader can tell what must match for replay without confusing it with where or when a run happened.

assumptions: accepted object refs and byte hashes are collision-free for the observed corpus
teaching_traceability.falsifier_or_refusal: Any attempt to place destination, receipt, publication time, or correction fact into the prior manifest fails.
teaching_traceability.honest_nonclaim: Immutability does not certify institutional endorsement or scientific truth.
teaching_traceability.math_or_proof: ObjectRef=(id,version,H_content) and ArtifactByteHash=H_art(bytes); changing content or bytes requires a new identity/version/hash.
teaching_traceability.ordinary_example: A signed receipt stays unchanged; a later note is stapled beside it rather than erasing the original total.
teaching_traceability.plain_meaning: Once an artifact or manifest is identified, later events point to it instead of editing it.
teaching_traceability.positive_value: The project keeps a durable audit trail of what was actually known and recorded at each stage.

assumptions: required artifact kinds and trace completeness were fixed prospectively
teaching_traceability.falsifier_or_refusal: A PRESENT/complete manifest with a missing artifact, mismatched hash, partial prefix, or absent terminal evidence fails.
teaching_traceability.honest_nonclaim: A complete manifest proves inventory closure, not correctness of its scientific conclusion.
teaching_traceability.math_or_proof: COMPLETE implies missing_required = empty and trace=COMPLETE; missing_required != empty implies manifest in {PARTIAL,UNRESOLVED}.
teaching_traceability.ordinary_example: A moving inventory with three of four boxes checked is partial even if the unchecked box's line is blank.
teaching_traceability.plain_meaning: A checklist missing a required item remains partial or unresolved; it is never treated as complete because an empty placeholder exists.
teaching_traceability.positive_value: Downstream readers can safely distinguish usable complete evidence from honestly incomplete evidence.

teaching_traceability.falsifier_or_refusal: Missing artifact, hash mismatch, ambiguous prefix, wrong run, wrong authority, or different destination bytes fails.
teaching_traceability.honest_nonclaim: I-8 proves no real crash consistency because UQ-26 remains open.
teaching_traceability.math_or_proof: H_art(source)=recorded_hash and destination is absent or destination_bytes=source_bytes; recovered_ref=original_ref.
teaching_traceability.ordinary_example: Restoring a scanned contract is acceptable only when every byte matches the recorded fingerprint; a retyped version is a different document.
teaching_traceability.plain_meaning: Recovery can reattach only the exact bytes already evidenced for the exact run and prefix; different bytes belong to a separately authorized corrected-object relation.
teaching_traceability.positive_value: Operational restoration cannot quietly become a rerun, scientific recomputation, correction, or overwrite.

assumptions: the store is the sealed in-memory dummy type
teaching_traceability.falsifier_or_refusal: A structural store substitute, wrong key/hash, wrong authorization, different bytes, or mismatched receipt fails.
teaching_traceability.honest_nonclaim: No network/filesystem destination, durable backend, mirror, or production publication protocol is accepted.
teaching_traceability.math_or_proof: key=H_art(bytes); put(key,b)=WRITTEN_ONCE if absent, ALREADY_IDENTICAL if stored=b, otherwise ALREADY_EXISTS_DIFFERENT.
teaching_traceability.ordinary_example: A locker numbered by a package fingerprint may be filled once; the same package can be confirmed, but a different package cannot replace it.
teaching_traceability.plain_meaning: The inert store writes an absent content-address once, accepts already identical bytes, and refuses different bytes.
teaching_traceability.positive_value: Publication evidence can be tested without risking an external destination or rewriting an artifact.

teaching_traceability.math_or_proof: history_after = history_before || CorrectionRecord(original_ref,replacement_ref), with original_ref != replacement_ref and H(original_bytes) != H(replacement_bytes).
teaching_traceability.ordinary_example: A newspaper posts an erratum that names yesterday's article; it does not replace every archived copy as though the error never existed.
teaching_traceability.plain_meaning: A correction is a new forward-time linked fact and corrected object relation, never an eraser, negation, recovery operation, or physical-history rewrite.
teaching_traceability.positive_value: The framework preserves what was originally known, shows what changed and why, supports reproducible audit, and supplies an immutable substrate for a separately authorized later correction-feedback programme.
